title: Same-day sediment cut total phosphorus error more than orthophosphate error at two Gulf river outlets in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether measured suspended sediment adds more concentration information for total phosphorus than for filtered orthophosphate. We used USGS version 3.0 Sample records at two related Gulf river outlets and 729 held-out site-dates in water years 2000-2025. Fits used the previous 20 years and accounted for flow, season and time. Adding same-day sediment cut total phosphorus squared log error by 23.87% and raised orthophosphate error by 1.42%. The difference in gains was 25.29 percentage points, with a conditional 95% three-year block interval of 16.08 to 38.36. Expanding history reduced the difference to 12.06 points, with an interval of 4.29 to 19.51. This is consistent with useful particle-related information, but does not isolate particle phosphorus or prove a physical cause. Current sediment is assumed known. Sparse dates, censor exclusions, related branches, source revision and conditional uncertainty limit use. The package includes numerical extracts from CC0 source data, hashes, code, predictions, aggregate evidence, a figure and an independent numerical audit.

display.caption: Added sediment reduced total phosphorus error more than filtered orthophosphate error on matched test dates. Bars show conditional 95% three-year block intervals. Annual error differences are negative when sediment helps.
